title: Thermal Energy and Temperature
seo_title: Grade 6 Thermal Energy Worksheets: Temperature, Mass and Type of Material
standard_text: Plan an investigation to determine the relationships among the energy transferred, the type of matter, the mass, and the change in the average kinetic energy of the particles as measured by the temperature of the sample.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on thermal energy and temperature (NGSS MS-PS3-4): average kinetic energy, how mass and material affect temperature change, and heating data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: The same energy changes temperature differently.
key_sub: Less mass or a different material can mean a bigger temperature change. Temperature is the average energy of particles.
body_html:
How to think about it

Temperature measures the average motion (kinetic energy) of particles. Thermal energy is the total energy of all the particles.

When the same amount of energy is added:

  • Less mass changes temperature more; more mass changes temperature less.
  • Different materials change temperature by different amounts (sand heats faster than water).
  • More energy added means a bigger temperature change.

A bathtub of warm water has more thermal energy than a cup of hot tea, even though the tea has a higher temperature.

Example

Same heat to 100 g and 400 g of water. Which warms more?

Less mass, bigger change.

Answer: the 100 g

Example

A cup and a pot of soup are both 60 °C. Which has more thermal energy?

Same temperature.

The pot has more particles.

Answer: the pot

Common mistakes

  • Thinking temperature and thermal energy are the same thing.
  • Thinking all materials heat up the same way.
  • Changing more than one variable in an investigation.

faq.q: What is the difference between temperature and thermal energy?
faq.a: Temperature is the average kinetic energy of the particles. Thermal energy is the total energy of all the particles.

faq.q: How does mass affect temperature change?
faq.a: With the same energy added, a smaller mass changes temperature more than a larger mass.

faq.q: Why does sand get hotter than water in the sun?
faq.a: Different materials change temperature by different amounts. Sand warms up much faster than water.

items.q: Why does sand on a beach get hot faster than the ocean water?
c: Sand changes temperature more easily than water with the same energy.
items.e: Different materials change temperature differently.

items.q: Emma compares two things. Which has a higher temperature: a swimming pool (25 °C) or a pot of boiling water (100 °C)?
items.e: Temperature measures the average motion of the particles.

items.q: Two pots of water get the same amount of heat. Pot A has 1 kg and pot B has 2 kg. Which warms up more?
items.e: Less mass means a bigger temperature change.

items.q: Ruby compares two things. Which has more total thermal energy: a swimming pool (25 °C) or a pot of boiling water (100 °C)?
c: They have the same thermal energy.
items.e: Thermal energy is the total energy of all the particles; the larger amount has far more particles.

items.q: Energy is transferred from a hot stove to a pot of water. What happens to the stove's particles near the pot?
items.e: Energy moves from hotter to cooler.
